sources.title: George Hatke, Between Interconnectedness and Insularity: Soqotra
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study reconstructs Socotra, Banu Afrar rule, Qishn conflict, Portuguese contact, products, religion, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Sana’a Center, Yemen’s Al-Mahra: From Isolation to the Eye of a Geopolitical Storm
sources.note: Modern policy history distinguishes Mahri identity, Banu Afrar political tradition, Qishn, tribal consultation, and later state forms.

sources.title: Polish Academy of Sciences journal record for Hatke’s Socotra study
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article record and text document sixteenth-century missions and Socotran students at Goa.

sources.title: UNESCO nomination history and development of Socotra
sources.note: World Heritage documentation dates Banu Afrar rule on Socotra to 1480 and carefully notes major historical uncertainties.

sources.title: Portuguese Expansion Virtual Encyclopedia: Socotra
sources.note: University encyclopedia covers Banu Afrar occupation, Portuguese rule, subsistence constraints, retreat, and later maritime calls.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Islam entry: Kishm
sources.note: Scholarly reference covers Qishn, Banu Afrar, Kathiri attack, Portuguese intervention, and later town economy.

sources.title: The Portuguese in the Sea of Oman, volume 7, page 215
sources.note: Edited documentary chronology records a 1545 letter concerning Qishn and Portuguese-Mahri diplomacy.

sources.title: The Portuguese in the Sea of Oman, volume 8, page 480
sources.note: Edited documentary chronology identifies Alvaro de Castro’s 5 April 1548 report on Qishn.

sources.title: The Portuguese in the Sea of Oman, volume 8, page 481
sources.note: Edited documentary chronology lists follow-up July 1548 correspondence about occupation of Qishn.

sources.title: Qatar Digital Library: East India Company third voyage to Socotra
sources.note: Archive essay summarizes the 1608 voyage, Tamrida encounter, gifts, commodities, and uneven relations.

sources.title: William Hawkins journal, Socotra landing, folio 25 recto
sources.note: Digitized primary journal page records April 1608 landing, navigation, places, weather, and exchange.

sources.title: William Hawkins journal, folio 14 recto
sources.note: British Library manuscript metadata anchors the 1608 voyage and its dated Socotra observations.

sources.title: Journal of the Clove at Socotra, 1612
sources.note: Digitized East India Company journal provides a separate February 1612 Socotra call.

sources.title: Library of Congress, John Jourdain journal, 1608 to 1617
sources.note: Digitized travel journal records Company voyages through Socotra, Aden, and Mocha during the early seventeenth century.

sources.title: Ingo Strauch, Indian inscriptions from the cave Hoq on Socotra
sources.note: Epigraphic study places Gujarati visitor inscriptions in seventeenth- and eighteenth-century Indian Ocean mobility.

sources.title: Heritage: Gujarati inscriptions of Socotra
sources.note: University study catalogs Gujarati inscriptions and treats them as evidence of visitors and traders.

sources.title: Heritage: Socotra and early modern Indian Ocean trade
sources.note: University study relates sixteenth- and seventeenth-century material traces to regional maritime commerce.

sources.title: Yemen and the Search for Stability
sources.note: Scholarly volume emphasizes fluid sultanic influence and warns that later British categories exaggerated centralized authority.

sources.title: Serge D. Elie, Communal Identity Transformation in Soqotra
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study examines Afrar dynastic legitimacy, local hierarchy, island society, and colonial transformation.

sources.title: University of Leeds, When Melodies Gather
sources.note: University project describes Mahri as traditionally oral and documents poetic historical memory.

sources.title: Journal of Semitic Studies: Mehri children’s rhymes and riddles
sources.note: Modern linguistic fieldwork documents children’s oral genres without projecting them unchanged into early modern life.

sources.title: Journal of Semitic Studies: Mehri oral poetry
sources.note: Modern fieldwork analyzes performance, memory, language, and social contexts of Mahri poetry.

sources.title: Mahri poetry and regional oral traditions
sources.note: Open academic record links Mahri oral poetry to historical memory and neighboring South Arabian traditions.

sources.title: University of Leeds, traditional ecopoetics in al-Mahrah
sources.note: Research project records modern poetry by men and women about desert, mountains, coast, and sea.

sources.title: SOAS ELAR: launch of the Mehri Center for Research and Studies
sources.note: Language-archive report describes community-led modern documentation and preservation of Mehri linguistic heritage.

sources.title: Endangered Languages Project, Mahri Poetry Archive
sources.note: Modern archive provides recordings and transcriptions while illustrating the recent documentation context.

sources.title: Lex Danish National Encyclopedia: Mehri
sources.note: Reference states that Mehri lacks a traditional written tradition and identifies an 1840 wordlist as its earliest surviving record.

sources.title: UNESCO, safeguarding Soqotri through a unified alphabet
sources.note: Official account dates standardized Soqotri alphabet work to the modern period, not the early modern sultanate.

sources.title: UNESCO, Nature and People in the Socotra Archipelago
sources.note: Official overview connects island livelihoods, biodiversity, pastoralism, and community knowledge in the present.

sources.title: UNESCO Socotra management plan
sources.note: Management documentation records modern pastoral movement, settlement, seasonal water, livelihoods, and conservation pressures.

sources.title: Journal of Ethnopharmacology: medicinal plants of Socotra
sources.note: Modern field data from 1990 documents medicinal-plant knowledge while offering no direct evidence for 1530 to 1715.

sources.title: Ethnobotany of Dracaena cinnabari resin
sources.note: Open research reviews dragon’s blood uses and explicitly combines historical reports with modern ethnobotany.

sources.title: Traditional medicinal plants of Socotra
sources.note: Open ethnobotanical study documents modern remedies and the need to avoid assuming unchanged historical practice.

sources.title: The Maritime Traditions of Socotra
sources.note: University thesis combines archaeology, texts, and modern fieldwork on boats, fishing, navigation, and coastal communities.

sources.title: Pastoralism on Socotra: continuity and change
sources.note: Peer-reviewed modern study analyzes herding, mobility, ecology, and household livelihood strategies.

sources.title: Socotran pastoralism and external entanglements
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study examines island pastoralists’ exchanges, institutions, and changing outside relationships.

sources.title: Aleksandr Sedov, Monuments of Socotra
sources.note: Archaeological survey describes built remains and cautions against simple narratives drawn only from later travel accounts.

sources.title: Qatar Digital Library, Qishn route and settlement, 1915
sources.note: Later gazetteer records wells, fishing, pastoralism, trade, and imported foods at Qishn; used only as later comparison.

sources.title: Gazetteer of Arabia, Qishn and Socotra entry
sources.note: Later colonial gazetteer describes Afrar authority and mainland-island representation, not early modern uniform control.

sources.title: Gazetteer of Arabia, Mahra regional links
sources.note: Later reference locates Qishn and records ties among Mahra, Hadramawt, and Dhofar.

sources.title: Qatar Digital Library, status of Socotra papers
sources.note: Twentieth-century archive demonstrates the later administrative construction of a two-part mainland-island state.

sources.title: Sana’a Center, tribal traditions and customary law in al-Mahra
sources.note: Modern research documents mediation and customary norms while warning against timeless assumptions.

sources.title: University of Leeds, documenting Mehri biocultural knowledge
sources.note: Research report explains modern collaborative documentation of language, poetry, plants, weather, and environment.

sources.title: Royal Asiatic Society study of the Mehri participle
sources.note: Modern linguistic analysis confirms Mehri’s distinct grammar but does not supply an early modern written sample.
